about: Historical scale for the stability meter. Each era is a snapshot of its most intense ~two weeks, scored with the SAME rubric as today's events (ORACLE.md section 3: chaos, polarization, economic 1-10; institutional resistance 1-10; age = days before the snapshot date) plus the big dates that were coming up (calendar: kind + days away). tools/core.py runs them through the SAME volatility formula as today, so their V values sit on the same ruler. Scored retrospectively by Claude on 2026-10-14, which means with hindsight. Rule: never re-score an era to make it fit; add new eras instead.

eras.name: Victorian Britain at its height
eras.like: Peace, booming trade and railways, and the Great Exhibition showing off the empire's confidence. Political fights were about religion and reform, not survival.
eras.next: Decades of relative stability and growth followed; reform came gradually through Parliament.

events.title: Great Exhibition opens in the Crystal Palace
Steady growth from railways and trade
Parliament fights over the anti-Catholic Ecclesiastical Titles Bill
Chartist reform movement fades after 1848

eras.name: Postwar calm
eras.like: Near-full employment, low inflation and a popular president running on 'peace and prosperity.' The big tension was school desegregation, where the National Guard was sent to some towns.
eras.next: Eisenhower won in a landslide. The civil-rights struggle grew slowly through the late 1950s.

events.title: Eisenhower campaigns for re-election on peace and prosperity
Desegregation standoffs in Clinton, Tennessee and Mansfield, Texas; National Guard called in
Steel industry back to work after summer strike
Suez Canal tension after Egypt nationalizes the canal
Economy near full employment with low inflation

eras.name: Cuban Missile Crisis
eras.like: Thirteen days where nuclear war felt possible. Fear was enormous, but the country rallied behind the president and institutions held firm.
eras.next: The Soviets withdrew their missiles. A hotline and a test-ban treaty followed. Kennedy's party did well in the midterms.

events.title: US spy plane shot down over Cuba; nuclear war feared
Soviet ships approach the naval quarantine line
Stocks fall on war fears
Kennedy announces naval quarantine of Cuba
Congress and public rally behind the president

eras.name: 1968: assassinations, riots and Vietnam
eras.like: Two national leaders assassinated in two months, riots in over 100 cities, a war tearing the country apart, and campus protests everywhere.
eras.next: Chaotic Democratic convention in August; Nixon won on 'law and order.' The war and the protests went on for years.

events.title: Robert F. Kennedy assassinated after winning the California primary
Rising inflation and Vietnam War spending strain the budget
Vietnam casualties near their peak; protests on campuses
Poor People's Campaign encamped on the National Mall
Cities still scarred by riots after Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination

eras.name: Watergate: Nixon resigns
eras.like: A president forced out by scandal, with inflation above 10% and stocks in a bear market. Yet it was orderly: courts, Congress and the press all did their jobs.
eras.next: Ford took over peacefully and pardoned Nixon. Democrats won big in the midterms, and the economy fell into recession.

events.title: Nixon resigns ahead of certain impeachment
Ford sworn in; peaceful transfer of power
Inflation above 10%; stocks in a bear market
'Smoking gun' tape released
House committee approves articles of impeachment

eras.name: Iran hostage crisis and stagflation
eras.like: Inflation above 12%, the Fed hiking rates sharply, gas worries, and Iran holding Americans hostage. A widespread feeling that things were slipping out of control.
eras.next: The hostage crisis lasted 444 days. A recession hit in 1980, and Carter lost in a landslide to Reagan.

events.title: Carter halts Iranian oil imports; gas worries return
Mortgage rates hit records after the Fed's sharp rate hikes
Inflation runs above 12%
Ted Kennedy launches a primary challenge to the president
Militants seize the US embassy in Tehran and take hostages

eras.name: Britain's Winter of Discontent
eras.like: Waves of strikes: trucks stopped, garbage piled in the streets, some of the dead went unburied. Inflation was back and the government looked powerless.
eras.next: The government lost a confidence vote in March, and Thatcher won the election in May, starting a sharp change of direction.

events.title: Public-sector strikes: rubbish piles up, some dead go unburied
Truck drivers' strike causes shortages
Inflation back above 9%; government pay caps collapse
'Crisis? What crisis?' headline sums up the prime minister's response

eras.name: Late-1990s boom
eras.like: Low unemployment, record stock markets and a bipartisan budget deal. The headlines were a big but orderly strike and fundraising hearings.
eras.next: The boom continued to 2000. The biggest political drama was the 1998 impeachment, which the system absorbed.

events.title: Stock market near record highs; unemployment under 5%
Senate hearings on 1996 campaign fundraising
Teamsters strike shuts down UPS deliveries
Clinton signs bipartisan balanced-budget deal

eras.name: 9/11 attacks
eras.like: The deadliest attack on US soil, the airspace shut for days, and the stock market's worst week in decades. But the country pulled together and institutions held.
eras.next: War in Afghanistan within a month, a short recession, and a long era of security politics.

events.title: Stock market reopens and falls 7%
National unity; the president's approval surges
Congress passes use-of-force resolution almost unanimously
All US airspace shut down for days
Terrorist attacks kill nearly 3,000 people

eras.name: 2008 financial crisis
eras.like: The biggest bank failure in US history, credit markets frozen, Congress first voting down the bailout and the market crashing, all five weeks before an election.
eras.next: The bailout passed, Obama won, and the Great Recession deepened into 2009 before a slow recovery.

events.title: Congress passes $700 billion bank rescue
Credit markets freeze; companies can't borrow
House rejects the bailout; stocks plunge 7%
Washington Mutual seized: largest bank failure in US history

eras.name: Debt-ceiling showdown
eras.like: Congress came within hours of a US default, the country lost its AAA credit rating, and stocks fell sharply. Unemployment was still stuck above 9%.
eras.next: No default. Years of budget brinkmanship followed, but the recovery continued slowly.

events.title: Stocks fall 5.6% in a day
S&P strips the US of its AAA credit rating
Unemployment stuck at 9.1%
Debt-ceiling deal reached hours before default deadline

eras.name: Kavanaugh fight before the 2018 midterms
eras.like: A bitterly divided Supreme Court confirmation with mass protests at the Capitol, but a strong economy with the lowest unemployment since 1969.
eras.next: Democrats won the House a month later. The economy kept growing until the pandemic.

events.title: Kavanaugh confirmed 50-48 after assault allegations
Unemployment falls to 3.7%, lowest since 1969
Mass protests at the Capitol; hundreds arrested
Trade-war tariffs on China escalate

eras.name: Pandemic and George Floyd protests
eras.like: 100,000 dead from COVID, 40 million jobless claims, and protests and riots in hundreds of cities with curfews and troops. The most turbulent stretch in decades.
eras.next: Protests faded over the summer, the economy rebounded with huge aid, and a bitterly contested election came in November.

events.title: Federal forces clear Lafayette Square; troop deployment threatened
Protests and riots in hundreds of cities after George Floyd's killing; curfews
Jobless claims top 40 million since March
US COVID deaths pass 100,000
Fed and Congress pour trillions into the economy

eras.name: January 6 Capitol attack
eras.like: A mob stormed the Capitol to stop the count of electoral votes, during the deadliest days of the pandemic. Congress finished the count that same night.
eras.next: Biden was inaugurated peacefully two weeks later. Trump was impeached a second time and acquitted.

events.title: Congress certifies the election overnight
COVID deaths hit a record of about 4,000 a day
Mob storms the Capitol to stop the electoral count
Georgia runoffs flip control of the Senate
Recording of pressure call to Georgia's secretary of state released

eras.name: Great Depression bank panic
eras.like: The banking system was collapsing, a quarter of workers were jobless, and farmers were rioting over foreclosures.
eras.next: FDR closed every bank for a week, launched the New Deal, and confidence slowly returned, though the Depression lasted years.

events.title: FDR inaugurated: 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself'
Banking system collapses; states declare bank holidays
Unemployment near 25%
Farm foreclosure riots in the Midwest

eras.name: Weimar Germany's hyperinflation
eras.like: Money became worthless (a loaf of bread cost billions), food riots broke out, regions tried to break away, and Hitler attempted a coup in Munich.
eras.next: A new currency stopped the inflation and calm returned for a few years, but the damage to trust helped the Nazis rise after 1929.

events.title: The mark collapses: a loaf of bread costs billions
New currency (Rentenmark) introduced
Food riots in German cities
Hitler's Beer Hall Putsch fails in Munich
Separatist revolts in the Rhineland

eras.name: Soviet Union: the August coup
eras.like: Hardliners tried to seize power with tanks in Moscow, crowds defended parliament, republics declared independence, and shelves were empty.
eras.next: The coup failed in three days, and the Soviet Union dissolved within four months.

events.title: Coup collapses after three days
Baltic republics declare independence
Hardliners attempt a coup; tanks in Moscow
Yeltsin defies the coup; crowds defend parliament
Shortages and rationing across the country

eras.name: French Revolution: storming of the Bastille
eras.like: A bankrupt state, bread at record prices, the king massing troops around Paris, and then crowds seizing the Bastille.
eras.next: The monarchy lost control within weeks. A decade of revolution, terror and war followed.

events.title: Crowd storms the Bastille
King dismisses popular finance minister Necker
Bread prices at a 70-year high; hunger in Paris
Royal troops mass around Paris
State bankruptcy looms

eras.name: Outbreak of the US Civil War
eras.like: Seven states had left the Union, trade between North and South had collapsed, and then Confederate guns fired on Fort Sumter.
eras.next: Four more states seceded, and four years of war killed over 600,000 Americans.

events.title: Lincoln calls for 75,000 volunteers
Confederates fire on Fort Sumter; war begins
Banks and trade between North and South collapse
Seven states have seceded; more are about to follow

eras.name: Roman Republic: Caesar crosses the Rubicon
eras.like: Decades of street violence between political gangs, a Senate trying to strip a general of his army, and the general marching on Rome instead.
eras.next: Civil war. The Republic never recovered; within two decades Rome was ruled by emperors.

events.title: Caesar crosses the Rubicon with his army: civil war
Tribunes loyal to Caesar flee Rome
Senate orders Caesar to disband his army
Years of gang warfare in Rome's streets
